source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 4 / line 6 Pension and Annuity Subtraction (PDF p.18-19 Line 4 bullets; p.19-20 Line 6; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 4 and 6) ('should not be intermingled between spouses'); DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5), joint federal AGI over 95,000; DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (spouse) 100,000.00 + private pension (spouse) 15,000.00 + IRA distribution (you) 10,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 150,500.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 30,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 15,000.00 + other income 125,000.00 = 140,000.00; less 32,000.00 = 108,000.00; line 11 = 96,000.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 108,000.00 and 12,000.00 = 6,000.00; line 14 = 6,000.00; line 15 = 85% x 96,000.00 = 81,600.00; line 16 = 87,600.00; 85% of benefits = 25,500.00; taxable Social Security = 25,500.00. Federal taxable income = 150,500.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 119,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 119,000.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 150,500.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 119,000.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 62, 55-64): federal AGI (DR 0104 line 34) 150,500.00 exceeds 95,000.00, so the full subtraction is not allowed and the subtraction is limited to 20,000: smaller of 25,500.00 and 20,000.00 = 20,000.00. Line 4 (primary taxpayer, age 62, at least 55 but not yet 65): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 10,000.00; limit 20,000.00 minus line 3 20,000.00 = 0.00; subtraction = smaller of 10,000.00 and 0.00 = 0.00. Line 6 (secondary taxpayer, age 58, at least 55 but not yet 65): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 15,000.00; limit 20,000.00 minus line 5 0.00 = 20,000.00; subtraction = smaller of 15,000.00 and 20,000.00 = 15,000.00. Line 22 subtotal = 35,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 35,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 119,000.00 - 35,000.00 = 84,000.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 84,000.00 = 3,696.00 (taxable income over 50,000: the PDF p.35 worksheet multiplies by .044, same figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 3,696.00. Each spouse separately (PDF p.19 'Each spouse must meet the requirements for the subtraction separately'): the primary taxpayer's Social Security subtraction of 20,000.00 uses up their own 20,000 pension limit, so their IRA distribution gets nothing; the spouse's own 20,000 limit is not reduced by the primary taxpayer's Social Security and covers the spouse's 15,000.00 pension in full. The projection reduces the primary taxpayer's cap by their full taxable benefit 25,500.00 rather than by the 20,000.00 line 3 figure; both leave 0.00.
accepted_approximations: The pension cap is reduced by each person's taxable Social Security (the record's line 3 or line 5 subtraction). That equals the printed rule whenever the Social Security subtraction is the person's full taxable benefit, and also when it is limited to 20,000 (the 55-64 pension cap is then used up either way). How a joint return's taxable Social Security (Form 1040 line 6b) is split between spouses is left to a Department publication not in the sources; the projection splits it the way the household's facts do.
